questions.prompt: Describe a situation where a critical database performance bottleneck in a Node.js and TypeScript application impacted production. How did you diagnose, resolve, and prevent recurrence?

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
```

questions.prompt: Design a globally distributed idempotency key service for financial transactions processing millions of requests per second with strict consistency guarantees. Discuss how you handle race conditions when identical requests arrive concurrently.
questions.answer_outline:
1. Understand Requirements: Must handle high write throughput, exact-once execution semantics, low latency, and multi-region failover.
2. Architectural Approach: Use a distributed transactional key-value store (like DynamoDB with conditional writes) fronted by regional Node.js/TypeScript microservices.
3. Handling Race Conditions: Implement a distributed locking mechanism or pessimistic locking via database conditional expressions (attribute_not_exists) to reject concurrent duplicate requests.
4. Trade-offs: Strong consistency versus availability during partition events (CP vs AP system choices).
5. Mermaid Diagram:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Client
    participant API_Gateway
    participant NodeService as Node.js Service
    participant DB as DynamoDB
    Client->>API_Gateway: POST /v1/charges (Idempotency-Key: abc)
    API_Gateway->>NodeService: Forward Request
    NodeService->>DB: Conditional Write (Key: abc, Status: PROCESSING)
    alt Key Exists & Completed
        DB-->>NodeService: Return Cached Result
        NodeService-->>Client: 200 OK (Cached Response)
    else Key Exists & Processing
        DB-->>NodeService: ConditionalCheckFailedException
        NodeService-->>Client: 409 Conflict / Retry-After
    else New Key
        DB-->>NodeService: Success
        NodeService->>NodeService: Execute Payment Logic
        NodeService->>DB: Update Key Status (Status: COMPLETED, Result: payload)
        NodeService-->>Client: 200 OK (Fresh Response)
    end
```

questions.prompt: Design a high-throughput serverless webhook delivery system using AWS Lambda, SQS, and API Gateway that guarantees at-least-once delivery with exponential backoff and dead-letter queueing.
questions.answer_outline:
1. Requirements: Outbound webhook dispatch to thousands of merchant endpoints with varying latency and failure rates.
2. Components: API Gateway ingestion, Amazon SQS FIFO/Standard queues for buffering, AWS Lambda consumers for batch processing and HTTP dispatch, and DynamoDB for tracking delivery attempts.
3. Retry Strategy: Implement exponential backoff with jitter inside Lambda execution before pushing back to SQS visibility timeout or moving to a DLQ.
4. Security & Observability: HMAC signature generation for payloads, CloudWatch metrics for latency and failure alerts.
5. Mermaid Diagram:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Event Trigger] -->|Enqueue| B(SQS Queue)
    B -->|Batch Poll| C[AWS Lambda Dispatcher]
    C -->|HTTP POST + HMAC| D[Merchant Endpoint]
    D -- Success --> E[Acknowledge SQS Message]
    D -- Failure --> F{Retry Count Exceeded?}
    F -- No --> G[Increase Backoff & Requeue]
    F -- Yes --> H[Send to DLQ]
```

questions.prompt: Design an event-driven architecture using Kafka or AWS SNS/SQS for processing real-time asynchronous merchant payouts. Explain how you ensure message ordering and handle consumer lag during traffic spikes.
questions.answer_outline:
1. Context: Payout ledger updates must be processed sequentially per merchant account to prevent balance corruption.
2. Partitioning Strategy: Use merchant_id as the partition key in Kafka to guarantee strict ordering of events per merchant.
3. Scalability & Lag Management: Consumer group scaling, auto-scaling based on consumer lag metrics, and backpressure handling.
4. Idempotency & Recovery: Offset management, at-least-once processing, and compensating transactions for failed downstream banking APIs.
5. Mermaid Diagram:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Payout API] -->|Produce Event| B[Kafka Topic: Payouts]
    B -->|Partition by Merchant ID| C1[Consumer 1]
    B -->|Partition by Merchant ID| C2[Consumer 2]
    C1 -->|Ledger Update| D[PostgreSQL DB]
    C2 -->|Ledger Update| D
    C1 -.->|Lag Alert| E[CloudWatch Monitor]
```

questions.prompt: Design a multi-tenant global ledger database schema supporting double-entry bookkeeping for millions of businesses. Discuss sharding strategies and maintaining ACID properties across distributed shards.
questions.answer_outline:
1. Requirements: Strict financial invariants (sum of debits equals credits), high write throughput, tenant isolation.
2. Schema Design: Immutable ledger entries table, account balance table with optimistic concurrency control.
3. Sharding Strategy: Tenant-based sharding or hash-based sharding on account_id. Cross-shard transactions managed via Saga pattern or two-phase commit where necessary.
4. Performance Optimization: Append-only writes, indexing strategy, and archival partitioning for historical data.
5. Mermaid Diagram:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Client Request] -->|Route by Tenant ID| B[API Service]
    B -->|Saga Coordinator| C[Shard A: Ledger Entries]
    B -->|Saga Coordinator| D[Shard B: Account Balances]

    D --> E
```

questions.prompt: Design a distributed audit logging and compliance tracking system capable of ingesting petabytes of transaction logs with immutable storage and sub-second querying capabilities.
questions.answer_outline:
1. Requirements: Append-only immutability, tamper-proof cryptographic hashing (Merkle trees), fast search capabilities for compliance audits.
2. Pipeline: Fluentbit log collection -> Kafka buffer -> S3 Glacier / Parquet format for long-term cold storage + Elasticsearch / OpenSearch for fast indexing.
3. Security: Encryption at rest (KMS), role-based access control (RBAC), and write-once-read-many (WORM) storage policies.
4. Monitoring: Log pipeline drop detection and alerts on storage write failures.
5. Mermaid Diagram:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Microservices Fleet] -->|JSON Logs| B[Fluentbit Daemonset]
    B -->|Stream| C[Kafka Audit Topic]
```
